correctness.rationale: For the ten-transposition word metric, a move changes cycle count by one and each length-l cycle factors into l−1 transpositions. The central powered-distance matrix has the stated nontrivial block coefficients and multiplicities. I independently formed the four exact 120×120 distance-layer matrices: integer-scaled Lagrange projections for the distinct transposition adjacency eigenvalues 10, 5, 2, 0, −2, −5, −10 sum to the identity after unscaling, have ranks 1,16,25,36,25,16,1, and give the stated four layer scalars on each block. The −10 block is the sign direction. Six-term rational logarithm bounds make g(0), g′(0) and the comparison coefficient in g″ strictly positive for g=2^(−p)F′; the independent rational endpoint bound gives F(8/25)>13773/500000 and 2^(8/25)<5/4. Thus F crosses once, and the five other multipliers are strictly negative up to that crossing by the inequalities in RESULT.md:68–78. Double centering gives ranks 119 and 118; the Gaussian on the resulting distinct Euclidean points is strictly positive definite. Beyond the cutoff the sign-vector quadratic form has a negative first-order term as t decreases to zero, while 119e^(−t)<1 suffices for large-t strict positive definiteness. value.rationale: All transpositions give the canonical conjugation-invariant word metric on S5. The first spectral crossing and its multiplicity are needed for exact squared-Euclidean embedding ranks and describe which metric powers permit Gaussian kernels at every bandwidth. Determining the controlling sign direction rather than merely bounding one block gives a complete and usable invariant of this natural finite metric.
